fd543cb36d7ed24db4e6054a23fe4d0004359f4a.summary: An overview article, part 1 of 2, on user-mode dynamic hooking: placing hooks at runtime to intercept and redirect program execution. It covers IAT hooking, LD_PRELOAD library hooking, inline hooking and the Microsoft Detours framework, and notes uses in tracing, HIDS/HIPS, reverse engineering and rootkits.

Inline hooking can be used in user mode, although similar techniques can also work in kernel mode.

hedges: The article assumes the reader already has sufficient access to modify a program's memory to place a hook.

fdf53fac0af9cced76179fb1b9df0ce009952e36.summary: ESRC malware analysis (February 2022) of a malicious Word document disguised as a customer-center guide from Klip, a digital asset wallet service. When users enable content, macros run, drop an XML file that executes, and attempt to contact a command server. The server could not be reached, so analysis stopped there. The report links the threat to the Smoke Screen campaign and to Thallium (also known as Kimsuky), and describes the actor as North Korea-linked. It is currently detected as Trojan.Downloader.DOC.Gen.

It names ransomware groups and tools that it says use this attack vector, including LockBit, BlackCat and Akira. It then sets out defensive guidance on monitoring, backups, authentication, hardening and network restrictions.

After the May 2021 Colonial Pipeline incident, the group kept distributing malware and launched the BlackMatter ransomware-as-a-service. CrowdStrike Intelligence assesses CARBON SPIDER is highly likely behind BlackMatter, citing extensive technical overlaps with Darkside. The report lists BlackMatter victims across the Americas, Asia and Europe, and says ransom notes direct victims to a portal hosted on Tor.

fd935612ea036144030f0ca7fce0810b09c6eec4.summary: Cybereason's report on Operation Cobalt Kitty, an advanced persistent threat that targeted a global corporation. It describes spear-phishing, Cobalt Strike Beacon payloads, the Denis and Goopy backdoors (using DNS tunneling and DLL hijacking), an Outlook macro used as a command channel, and credential dumping. More than 35 machines were compromised. The report links the activity to the OceanLotus Group but frames this as a suspicion based on behavioural fingerprints.

fd349ea92882be4865ac41e962eba514af0eda06.summary: This is a how-to page describing the grsecurity RBAC access control system: its policy file, roles, subjects, objects, capability, resource and network rules, and sample policies. It documents a defensive product and does not report a threat, actor, campaign, malware or vulnerability, so no threat facts are recorded.
